title: Query Your Way Out: Benchmarking Multi-Turn Knowledge Reasoning through Generalized Puzzle Solving
abstract: arXiv:2610.16133v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Puzzles offer a natural testbed for Large Language Models (LLMs) reasoning because they pose verifiable goals under partial information and require multi-step decisions to reach a solution. However, existing puzzle benchmarks typically focus on narrow environments with rigid mechanics and tightly constrained solution targets. To bridge this gap, we introduce the Active Probing Benchmark (APB), which generalizes puzzle-solving by casting concept identification as an interactive reasoning task that integrates specialized knowledge assessment into the puzzle setting. Specifically, APB evaluates whether models can acquire information via multi-turn active probing and inference to pinpoint 960 target concepts of specialized difficulty across eight diverse academic domains. Our evaluation reveals a counter-intuitive phenomenon: most open-source reasoning models significantly underperform their standard instruction counterparts. This finding

translated_title: 以提问突围：通过广义谜题求解评测多轮知识推理能力
translated_abstract: 谜题为大型语言模型（LLM）的推理能力提供了一个天然的测试平台，因为谜题在信息不完整的情况下设定了可验证的目标，并且需要多步决策才能得出解决方案。然而，现有的谜题基准通常局限于机制固定、求解目标受到严格限制的狭窄环境。为弥合这一差距，我们提出了主动探测基准（Active Probing Benchmark, APB），它通过将概念识别转化为一种交互式推理任务来推广谜题求解，并将专业知识评估融入谜题设定之中。具体而言，APB 评估模型能否通过多轮主动探测与推理来获取信息，从而准确识别出涵盖八个不同学术领域的 960 个具有专业难度的目标概念。我们的评测揭示了一个反直觉的现象：大多数开源推理模型的表现显著落后于其对应的标准指令模型。这一发现……
tldr: 该论文提出了主动探测基准（APB），将概念识别转化为融合专业知识考核的交互式谜题求解任务，以评测大语言模型的多轮主动提问与知识推理能力，并发现开源推理模型的表现反而显著低于标准指令模型。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the Active Probing Benchmark (APB), which generalizes puzzle-solving as an interactive reasoning task integrating specialized knowledge assessment to evaluate LLMs' multi-turn active probing and knowledge reasoning, and reveals the counter-intuitive finding that open-source reasoning models significantly underperform their standard instruction counterparts.
